mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST QoQ < -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating average hourly earnings growth (implied by PAYEMS and UNRATE dynamics), signals a tight labor market that increases input costs and inflationary pressure, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate revenue prospects, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during four-month stretches where INDPRO is below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2% for three consecutive months signals an aggressive monetary easing cycle, which lowers borrowing costs and supports corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS < 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a precautionary savings regime, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS up AND GDPC1 down for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during episodes of rising RSAFS and falling GDPC1 for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during four-month stretches of monthly PAYEMS gains above 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% signals a stagflationary shock, which erodes real earnings and raises discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% and UNRATE > 5%.
